newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Red Cross ships 700 tonnes flour to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Red Cross ships 700 tonnes flour to N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross said on Wednesday it had shipped 700 tonnes of flour to famine-striken North Korea, the second such shipment in a week.
"We sent the food aid on a humanitarian basis and will continue to do so," said Red Cross spokesman Rhee Jong-keun.
"The ship carrying the flour left the port of Inchon at around midnight on Tuesday and will arrive at Nampo in the North late tonight," he added.
The flour, bought with donations from religious groups, was valued at 260 million won ($300,000), he said.
The aid shipment is the second since Pyongyang apologised last December for a submarine incursion that plunged ties to a new low.
Seoul froze all contacts with Pyongyang after a North Korean submarine landed 26 commandos on a Southern beach in September.
Shortly after the apology, Seoul returned the remains of 24 of the infiltrators who were shot and killed. One was captured alive and the other is still at large.
On Friday, the relief organisation shipped 300 tonnes of flour and 15,000 pairs of socks, worth a total of about $153,000, from Inchon.
North Korea, which has been suffering acute food shortages due to devastating floods in 1995 and 1996, said on Monday it had only half the grain needed to feed its people.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) described the food situation in flood-hit North Korea as critical and called for urgent aid.
The IFRC said it had raised less than a fifth of a $18 million emergency appeal for North Korea launched in November.
Last week, the IFRC said food rations in North Korea had dropped to four times lower than normally considered essential for a healthy population.

In January, Washington gave permission to Minneapolis-based Cargill Inc, the world's largest private grain trading company, to export 500,000 tonnes of wheat or rice to North Korea in what was expected to be a barter arrangement. ($1 = 869 won)
